Activities

PARC organizes research-oriented activities designed to help students explore artificial intelligence, machine learning, forecasting, and data science beyond traditional coursework.

Our activities focus on developing research skills, encouraging scientific discussions, and creating opportunities for collaboration.

Research Reading Groups

Learning through scientific literature

Reading research papers is one of the most important skills for becoming a researcher.

PARC reading groups provide a space for students to explore recent research papers, discuss ideas, and learn how scientific contributions are developed.

Topics may include:

  • probabilistic machine learning,
  • forecasting and time series,
  • statistical learning,
  • artificial intelligence,
  • data science applications.

Participants learn how to:

  • understand research papers,
  • analyse methodologies,
  • discuss limitations,
  • identify possible research directions.

Research Skills Workshops

Building the foundations for research

Research involves skills that are often learned through experience.

PARC workshops focus on practical aspects of research, including:

  • finding and reading scientific literature,
  • formulating research questions,
  • designing computational experiments,
  • reproducible research practices,
  • scientific communication.

Workshops may be delivered by researchers and collaborators from different academic backgrounds.

Collaborative Research Projects

Learning by doing

Research skills develop through practice.

PARC encourages small collaborative projects where students can explore ideas, reproduce existing work, and develop their understanding of research methodology.

Projects may involve:

  • implementing research methods,
  • analysing datasets,
  • exploring new approaches,
  • developing open-source tools.

The focus is on learning the research process rather than only achieving final results.

Research Talks and Discussions

Connecting with researchers

PARC hosts discussions with researchers and early-career scientists who share their experiences, research journeys, and perspectives on different areas of AI and data science.

These sessions provide students with insights into:

  • academic research,
  • graduate studies,
  • research careers,
  • current developments in the field.
